1.explanation: Both files implement the core rail‐mode collapse/expand logic. SideNav.js clones its children to pass down the navRailActive flag and contains the onFocus/onBlur handlers that should toggle expansion when focused (but currently no‐op when expanded is controlled externally). SideNavMenu.js watches navRailActive in componentDidUpdate to force its submenu into a collapsed state when the rail closes. The mismatch between controlled expanded state and these internal handlers causes the submenu UL to remain open (and not re-open on focus) in rail mode. Fixing this behavior requires adjusting SideNav.js to call the onToggle callback (or update internal state) on focus/blur even when controlled, and SideNavMenu.js to correctly respond to navRailActive in both directions.
1.bug_scenario: When the SideNav is rendered in “rail” mode (i.e. collapsed to show only icons) and a submenu inside it has been expanded, collapsing the rail leaves the submenu’s <ul> still open. The result is extra blank space (the hidden submenu area) and, if a submenu item had focus or was active, its :focus or :active styling shows even though the submenu items are visually hidden. Conversely, when the rail is fully collapsed and a user tabs into one of those hidden menu items, the rail should expand on focus and highlight the correct submenu item, but it doesn’t when the SideNav is controlled via the expanded prop.

2.explanation:
1. SideNav.js: This is the top-level component that implements rail mode, handles focus/blur toggles, and is responsible for passing the navRailActive flag into its immediate children. It only clones its direct children, so nested SideNavMenu components never actually receive navRailActive. It also treats controlled (expanded prop) mode differently, skipping internal state updates on focus without forcing the parent to toggle, so the rail doesn’t expand on keyboard focus.

2. SideNavItems.js: This wrapper component sits between SideNav and SideNavMenu in the tree. It currently renders children without forwarding the navRailActive prop or cloning its own children, breaking the intended navRailActive propagation pipeline from SideNav down to SideNavMenu.

3. SideNavMenu.js: This component implements the submenu collapse on rail close in componentDidUpdate by checking the navRailActive prop. Because navRailActive never arrives (see SideNav → SideNavItems), the submenu remains expanded when the rail collapses. It also never handles focus events itself, relying on SideNav, which in controlled mode does not update expanded without an onToggle callback.

To fix: SideNav.js (or SideNavItems.js) must propagate navRailActive to all nested SideNavMenu components, and SideNav.js should ensure onFocus/onBlur always toggles expanded in both controlled and uncontrolled modes (for example, by mandating an onToggle handler or updating its own state when isRail is true).
2.bug_scenario: When the UI Shell is in rail (collapsed) mode, open sub-menus do not collapse automatically, leaving empty whitespace where the hidden menu items sit. If one of those hidden submenu items is focused or active, its “current” styling still shows in the collapsed rail, creating a visual glitch. In addition, when the rail is controlled (expanded passed as a prop) and a user tabs into a submenu item, the rail does not auto-expand—even though SideNav has onFocus/onBlur logic—and the header menu button’s icon never updates to reflect the expanded state.
